clue.text: Workman holding broken bridle for Pope Gregory

indicators.note: a word that holds something keeps it inside, so the workman goes around the other piece

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of the harness word are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer carries a damaged harness strap on behalf of a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged harness word sits between the first letter and the rest of HAND, giving HILDEBRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Hildebrand was the birth name of the eleventh-century pontiff who reigned as Gregory VII.

clue.text: Middle East country filling pies cooked by Italian painter

indicators.note: a filling sits inside a pie, so the country is put within the other letters
cooked suggests the pastry has been altered by heat, so its letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a nation of the Middle East

explanation.surface: An Italian artist bakes pies with a Middle Eastern stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: By looks like it names the cook, but it only joins the wordplay to the artist. The country goes inside the reworked pastry word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Piranesi was an eighteenth-century Italian artist famed for his etchings of Rome and imaginary prisons.

clue.text: Emblem of French depravity

parts.note: de is the French word for of
vice is wickedness or depravity

explanation.surface: A symbol standing for the moral decadence of the French.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is a badge or symbolic design borne by a person or family.

clue.text: Fishes' fingerprints?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small flatfish found around British coasts
second meaning: British police slang for prints taken from fingers

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether fish leave prints.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that fish have no fingers; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a kind of flounder-like flatfish and is also informal British slang for fingerprints.

clue.text: Poem composed in even stages, perhaps

indicators.note: to compose something is to put it together, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem written in a series of regular steps or sections.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote The Eve of St Agnes and Tennyson wrote St Agnes' Eve; perhaps nods to the title being one example of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known Tennyson poem about a nun's vigil, closely echoing the Keats work.

clue.text: Acolyte badly hurt by firework

indicators.note: badly suggests the word has been damaged, so its letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: work here means to knead or shape, so the preceding letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the first half of firework, taken as written; its second half signals the reordering

explanation.surface: An altar server injured by a rocket or banger.
explanation.walkthrough: Firework splits into fire and work: the second half signals the shuffle of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurifer is the altar server who carries the thurible, or censer of incense, in church services.

clue.text: Article taken from Barbican turns out to be antacid

indicators.note: turns out suggests the remaining letters are turned around into a new order
taken from means removed out of, so the article is subtracted from the longer word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written; the Barbican is an arts centre in the City of London

explanation.surface: Something removed from a London arts venue proves to be an indigestion remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping AN leaves BARBIC, whose letters rearrange to BICARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarb, short for bicarbonate of soda, is taken to neutralise stomach acid and relieve heartburn.

clue.text: Ugly finish in untidy set is an eyesore

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
untidy means disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of ugly

explanation.surface: A messy television or furniture set looks horrible, a real blot on the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a sore swelling on the eyelid, so it is literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Vagrant I entertain out East?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their usual order
the compass point read with out means that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A tramp says he puts on shows wandering in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one E from I plus ENTERTAIN leaves nine letters that rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant travels from place to place without a settled home, like a wandering tramp.

clue.text: Part of flag — one among many

indicators.note: among puts one thing in the midst of others, so it goes inside

parts.note: a host is a great number of people or things
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item is one of a crowd making up a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside HOST, after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoist is the vertical edge of a banner nearest the staff, where it is hauled up.

clue.text: Records of air-conditioning in sideshow

indicators.note: in places the gas word inside the other one
conditioning means treating or reshaping, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the first half of sideshow, taken as written; its second half signals the reordering

indicators.note: show here hints that the letters are put on display in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Logs of the air-conditioning system installed at a fairground attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Air-conditioning wants to be a single compound noun; it splits into air and its rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaries are daily written accounts, a common form of personal record keeping.

clue.text: Time to dress in worthless stuff?

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Is it time to put on rubbishy clothes?
explanation.walkthrough: Time goes after dress; to means attached to.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage means rubbish or nonsense, anything of no value.

clue.text: Note always turning into another note

parts.note: B is a note in the musical scale

indicators.note: turning means the word is spun round to face the other way

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A musical note keeps changing into a different note.
explanation.walkthrough: B comes first, followed by the turned-round word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, equal to two semibreves.

clue.text: Fine imposed on fictitious tale is indescribable

indicators.note: in printing, to impose is to arrange the pages of type, so these letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a fable is an invented story

explanation.surface: A penalty slapped on a made-up story is beyond words.
explanation.walkthrough: Imposed reads as a penalty imposed; in printing it means arranging type, which reorders the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable means too great or extreme to be expressed in words.

clue.text: Certain line a boxer takes?

indicators.note: takes, like film takes, suggests another version of the same material, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The sure tactic a fighter adopts in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexorable means unstoppable, so its outcome is sure and unavoidable.

clue.text: Promise of employment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pledge, especially to marry
second meaning: a job or hiring for work

explanation.surface: A firm offer of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a formal pledge to wed and a contracted period of paid work, as for a performer.

clue.text: To one Pope, it spelt danger

definitions.text: To one Pope, it spelt danger

parts.words: To one Pope, it spelt danger
parts.note: surface reading: a pontiff sensing a threat
setter's reading: the poet Alexander Pope, who called a modest amount of knowledge a dangerous thing

explanation.surface: A pontiff reads an omen of peril.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope here is the eighteenth-century poet, not a pontiff; his Essay on Criticism has the famous line about shallow knowledge being dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope wrote that a slight amount of knowledge is a dangerous thing, so that is what spelt danger for him.

clue.text: Shrub found at river ski resort

parts.note: the Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it says to sort the letters again

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bush growing at a riverside winter sports centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday town; split as re-sort it orders a shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery-leaved bush often grown in coastal and dry regions.

clue.text: Lupine character with fixed semi-grin

indicators.note: fixed means repaired or rearranged, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wolfish figure wearing a frozen half-smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Isengrim is the wolf in the medieval fables of Reynard the Fox.

clue.text: Coped with some awful rot

indicators.note: awful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone managed to put up with a load of terrible nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Rot looks like a noun meaning nonsense; it is the verb to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To decompose is to decay or putrefy, which is what rotting matter does.

clue.text: Writer's cloak

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American author of In Cold Blood
second meaning: a long hooded cloak or overcoat

explanation.surface: The overcoat belonging to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was an American novelist, and a capote is also a long hooded mantle.

clue.text: Light soldier on animal's back

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A soldier riding on an animal's back.
explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like the animal's body part, but it turns the whole soldier-then-animal string round. GI is the usual crossword soldier, from the American term.
explanation.definitionFit: A kleig or klieg light is a powerful carbon-arc lamp used in film studios.

clue.text: Bears getting final put-down, unfortunately

parts.note: a knockout is the blow that floors a boxer for good
alas is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: Some bears suffer a crushing last insult, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Put-down suggests an insult; here it is the boxer put down for the count.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas are often called koala bears, though they are marsupials rather than true bears.

clue.text: Unusual poem about air in shops

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters appear in an unexpected order
about suggests letters moved around

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd piece of verse about the atmosphere of stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, the plural of emporium, are large retail stores selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Some other Semitic language

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A further tongue from the Hebrew and Arabic family.
explanation.walkthrough: Semitic language reads as one phrase, but only language is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Mixture the French found in turning over molten rock

indicators.note: turning over flips the whole thing to run the other way

parts.note: magma is molten rock beneath the earth's crust
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend of different elements, originally an alloy of mercury.

clue.text: Sailor wanted to be an ecclesiastic

parts.note: AB stands for able-bodied seaman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman longed to become a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbe is a French cleric, a title given to a priest or abbot in France.

clue.text: Locations where things worth seeing are reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

parts.note: sights are attractions worth viewing

explanation.surface: Places where the attractions are said to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are places or positions where something stands or happens.

clue.text: Bookkeeper's sign for rainstorm

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

parts.note: the first half of rainstorm, taken as written; its second half signals the reordering

explanation.surface: An accountant's zodiac sign predicts heavy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Bookkeeper suggests an accountant, but it is someone who looks after books in a library.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian is literally someone in charge of a collection of volumes.
